description:
Space exploration requires astronauts to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and decision-making skills to overcome challenges in space.

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, educational platform designed to introduce young learners to the exciting world of space exploration through realistic, mission-based simulations.
summary:
Junior Astronauts: Beyond the Stars (Space Kidz) is an interactive 3D space exploration game and autonomous lunar outpost trainer built by Xelorra Innovators for learners aged 7–12 under NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge 03).

Instead of passive trivia, young commanders operate Outpost Alpha at Shackleton Crater rim (89.9°S) and balance five interconnected survival systems in real time: closed-loop oxygen and water recycling (ECLSS), solar power with a 20% emergency battery lock, hydroponic space farming (1–4 bays), regolith radiation shielding, and a five-rover autonomous swarm (Scout, Digger, Hauler, Builder, Radio Relay) powered by live 2D A* detour pathfinding. Players click 3D lunar terrain to deploy beacons and direct rovers, assemble multi-stage rockets with animated liftoffs, explore eight 3D planets with moons, master 16 interactive Space Academy modules, and respond to real-time NOAA space-weather data inside an ad-free, musical web experience.
details: 1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS Junior Astronauts: Beyond the Stars (powered by Space Kidz) is a browser-based 3D STEM mission simulator and game built for children aged 7–12 (with selectable Young Explorer 7–9 and Advanced Explorer 10–12 modes). Rather than isolating facts in static quizzes, the app connects cosmic discovery directly to systems engineering on the Moon: - Explore Space (3D Solar System): Touch- and mouse-interactive Three.js planets (Mercury through Neptune) with Fresnel atmosphere shaders, axial tilt, Saturn’s rings, orbiting moons, science facts, game design ideas, and age-adapted discovery quizzes. - Rocket Builder & Mission Hub: 8 structured mission tracks, 3 playable Moon Base scenarios (Starter, Solar Storm Shield, Emergency Rescue), and a 4-stage interactive Rocket Assembly builder culminating in a live launchpad countdown and liftoff sequence. - Live 3D Lunar Outpost (Shackleton Crater Alpha, 89.9°S): Children manage competing lunar survival systems—Solar Array kW output and panel dust cleaning, a 1,200 kWh battery bank with a 20% emergency safety lock, closed-loop ECLSS oxygen (0.84 kg/crew/day) and water (>90% recycling), 1–4 hydroponic Space Farm bays, and a multi-layer regolith radiation shield wall protecting 4 crew members during solar storms. - Autonomous 5-Rover Swarm & Interactive Moon Terrain: Five specialized Three.js rovers—R1 Scout, R2 Digger, R3 Hauler, R4 Builder, and R5 Radio Relay—coordinate via a decentralized task auction and real-time 2D grid A* pathfinding to detour around boulders and craters. Players can click directly on 3D lunar terrain to drop Solar, Comms, and Scanner beacons or direct rovers, plus inspect any rover in 3D Normal/Thermal views and run manual repairs. - Space Academy & Progression: 16 interactive learning modules (12 core NASA science parameter labs + 4 deep-space modules across 10 topic tracks), Daily Challenges, 6 Astronaut Ranks, 8 earned badges, customizable suit gear, and a math-gated Parent/Teacher Area (7 × 4) with JSON learning-report exports and PPTX pitch export. 2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT - Builds authentic systems thinking early: Kids see immediate cause-and-effect consequences in plain language via a Decision Cause Log (for example, running all 4 Space Farm bays grows food faster but steals water and power needed for oxygen scrubbers and shield construction during a storm). - Accessible worldwide on low-bandwidth and school devices: Uses procedural Three.js textures, procedural Web Audio API soundscapes/rocket audio (zero heavy audio file downloads), and cached NOAA weather fallbacks so classrooms on Chromebooks, tablets, or phones get smooth performance. - Child-safe by design: Zero ads, zero third-party tracking, zero real-name or PII collection, math-gated caregiver reports, Reduced Motion toggle, on-screen audio captions, and age-adaptive voice guidance. 3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE USED - Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Motion animations, Lucide React icons. - 3D & Simulation Engine: Three.js (WebGL planets, moons, starfields, lunar craters, dynamic 5-layer regolith berm, rovers, beacons, thermal shader inspection), custom 2D grid A* pathfinder, task-auction swarm scheduler, and 1 Hz survival simulation engine. - Audio & Accessibility: Procedural Web Audio API cosmic ambient synth, kid-friendly background music, rocket liftoff roar, and tactile UI SFX, paired with Web Speech API voice coach and on-screen audio captions. - Backend & Exports: Node.js + Express (`server.ts`) proxying real-time NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) scales (`/api/space-weather`) with a 5-minute TTL cache and resilient offline fallback, plus PptxGenJS client-side presentation generation. 4. CREATIVITY & DESIGN FACTORS CONSIDERED - Visual & Audio Engagement: Deep-space cockpit aesthetic paired with kid-friendly Fredoka/Nunito typography, zero-clutter layout across mobile (390px) to 4K monitors, >= 48px touch targets, warm musical audio enabled out-of-the-box with volume controls, and voice-welcomed onboarding. - Honest Scientific Framing: Every science metric distinguishes "NASA-Derived Information" (e.g., Shackleton illumination, Apollo regolith density, OSDR storm dosimetry, ISS ECLSS rates) from gameplay "Simulation Assumptions" (accelerated rover speeds and harvest pacing so missions play in 2–5 minutes).
